subject.title: feat(linux): Quick Chat agent switcher, avatars, per-agent routing, and configurable shortcut

question: Should Linux Quick Chat be allowed to load arbitrary remote agent avatar URLs, and if so what URL schemes or origin restrictions are acceptable for the webview?
rationale: This is a product security and privacy boundary: a mechanical patch cannot determine whether configured identity data may cause arbitrary outbound image requests from the desktop companion.

options.title: Restrict avatar sources before merge
options.body: Allow only locally embedded/data avatars or a narrowly approved remote policy, and align `identityAvatarUrl` resolution and the webview CSP with that policy.

options.title: Accept remote avatar loading
options.body: Keep remote avatar support but explicitly document the accepted outbound-request and `http:`/`https:` trust model for Linux Quick Chat.

options.title: Defer remote avatars
options.body: Land the switcher and shortcut work without remote image loading, then revisit a shared cross-platform avatar-fetch policy separately.

recommendation.title: Restrict avatar sources before merge
recommendation.body: Allow only locally embedded/data avatars or a narrowly approved remote policy, and align `identityAvatarUrl` resolution and the webview CSP with that policy.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the Linux Quick Chat surface and its current integration with agent identity summaries.
